verdict.reason: All three cited locations exist exactly as quoted. .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:18-22 tells authors that "CI automatically posts a verification summary comment ... with per-lane results for both `verify:self` and `verify:integration`" and asks them to tick "verify:self — CI comment shows ✅" / "verify:integration — CI comment shows ✅"; CONTRIBUTING.md:101-103 repeats the contract ("posts a per-lane summary comment. The two checkboxes in the PR template must be green"). But ci-report.yml:288-292 states the comment is explicitly "Not whether the checks passed", and the body builder at ci-report.yml:319-354 emits only a scope heading, an optional "Lanes: N of M ran, K filtered" line, and a run link — no per-lane pass/fail, no ✅, and for verify-integration only a skipped/not-skipped signal derived from job conclusions (ci-report.yml:164-174). I confirmed no other producer of that comment exists: ci.yml posts nothing (its header at L32-46 records the move, and no createComment appears in it), and the `<!-- harness-verification -->` marker appears only in ci-report.yml:319 and in scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:9,122 where it is described as replaced as an evidence source. So the contributor-facing contract in two docs is unsatisfiable by the comment the workflow actually posts, and neither doc is reconciled — a real design-fit / doc-discipline mismatch of the unmet-requirement kind. No refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope) applies.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The reporter is now two github-script steps with two identities: ci-report.yml:97-103 reads on the ambient github.token, ci-report.yml:268-280 writes on steps.app-token.outputs.token. The entire rationale for that split lives only in YAML comments (ci-report.yml:87-96 and 265-267) plus scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:270-357, which itself says "The split is therefore only ever enforced by this test" (line 310). The canonical section "Reporting onto a fork PR" (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:318-395) still presents the reporter as one App-token unit ("the writes moved to a workflow_run-triggered reporter ... scoped to issues: write", 335-340), states only the no-checkout/no-pnpm invariant (342-345), says the whole "reporter degrades to the ambient token" (360) rather than writes-only, and nowhere states reads-on-ambient/writes-on-App nor the one-client-per-step and @actions/github-unresolvable constraint. Its sanitisation bullet still cites "forge table rows" (355) although the comment body now renders headings/bullets and no table (ci-report.yml:319-354). I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide .md greps for ambient, read step / write step, "#831", "Cannot find module", create-github-app-token, permission-issues, "binds ONE" / "one client per step", getOctokit returned only the pre-split narrative in harness-engineering.md, the task plan docs/tasks/active/20260812-path-aware-ci-todo.md (Phases 4b/4c/4d cover the fork-PR move, the label recompute and the globToRegExp drift guard; there is no phase for the token split - Phase 4d ends at line 237 and Phase 5 follows), and the review artifact .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:15. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-14 and 58-60 require writing or updating the existing design doc under docs/design/ for a non-trivial change, so leaving this security-relevant step-topology invariant recorded only in YAML comments and a test is a major design-doc-discipline violation in this lane.

This reports the SCOPE decision"), and the actual body-rendering block (ci-report.yml:319-354) emits no check-status table, no per-lane detail, no areas.full/areas.ciConfig phrasing, and no lane pass/fail line — only a gating-file block, a Reduced/Full/unknown heading, one aggregate "Lanes: N of M ran, K filtered" line, and a footer. The claimed downstream inconsistency is verifiable in the tree: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:18-22 promises "per-lane results for both verify:self and verify:integration" with two "CI comment shows ✅" checkboxes, CONTRIBUTING.md:101-103 promises "a per-lane summary comment" and says those checkboxes "must be green... before review", and scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:74-75 regenerates the same checkboxes into every agent-authored PR body. No other workflow posts such a comment (scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs prints to stdout for agent-iterate-ci.yml). docs/design/harness-engineering.md:308-314 does document the scope-only comment, which satisfies the design-doc-discipline half but confirms rather than refutes the purpose redefinition. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described (not not-present), nothing makes it unreachable (not already-guarded), and unrequested scope creep plus spec/doc inconsistency is explicitly inside the design-fit lens's lane (not out-of-scope). The originating issue's outcome/acceptance text was not available to me, so I could not establish that the redefinition was requested; that uncertainty keeps the finding.

The gating decision is recomputed independently from base-branch globs + `pulls.listFiles`, while the skip facts come from the run's job list; when the two disagree (exactly the case the resolver's fail-safe/diff-base bugs produce) the comment asserts scope that did not happen — contradicting the design intent stated three lines above the skipped computation ("it has to be what actually happened").
finding.evidence: ci-report.yml:322-343: `if (gatingFiles && gatingFiles.length > 0) { ... 'Full CI' }` precedes `else if (skipped.length > 0)`; ci-report.yml:156-163.

verdict.reason: The branch ordering exists as quoted (ci-report.yml:322-343), but the disagreement it is said to expose is unreachable, and the cited trigger does the opposite of what the finding assumes. (1) The heavy-job filter is on STEPS, not the job: verify-browser/verify-integration carry only "!cancelled() && needs.verify-self.result == 'success'" (ci.yml:324, 426) with the filter in RUN_HEAVY (ci.yml:338-341, 447-450), so a reduced or mis-resolved run still runs and expands both matrix jobs, which report success after no-oping (ci.yml:357-361, 479-483). scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:93-108 mechanically bans a job-level if referencing outputs.heavy/outputs.full/full-ci on those jobs. Since ci-report.yml:170-174 derives skipped from conclusion === 'skipped', skipped is empty on every reduced run, so the "else if (skipped.length > 0)" branch is never reached in the scenario described. (2) Every fail-safe route in scripts/changed-areas.mjs returns full: true, heavy: true while emitting ciConfig: false (440-447, 465-472, 485-492), so a fail-safe resolution runs the heavy jobs rather than skipping them; the "exactly the case the resolver's fail-safe/diff-base bugs produce" premise is false. (3) skipped is non-empty only when verify-self failed or was cancelled (ci.yml:324, 426); in that state the "Reduced CI ... add full-ci and re-run" text (ci-report.yml:336-339) would be the inaccurate one, while the gating-file branch accurately states the scope decision per the comment's stated purpose (ci-report.yml:288-292). ci-report.yml:156-163 governs the SOURCE of the skip facts, not branch precedence, so no stated design intent is contradicted. Separately, even read charitably this is message-precedence rendering logic (correctness lens), not an unmet acceptance criterion, a missing or parallel design doc (the behaviour is documented at docs/design/harness-engineering.md:357-359, 371-395), a duplicated module, or a Non-Goal breach.
